theme: John the Baptist; the baptism; the temptation
readingInstruction: Read Matthew 3:1-4:25. John prepares the way, Jesus is baptized, and the Father speaks. Then Jesus is led into the wilderness, where he is tempted, and he begins to call disciples. Watch how Jesus answers the devil.
settingTheScene: Jesus is about thirty years old when his public ministry begins. John the Baptist has been preaching in the Judean wilderness near the Jordan, calling Israel to repent in preparation for the king. Matthew presents what happens at the Jordan and in the wilderness as the start of a new exodus: Israel passed through the sea and was tested for forty years, and now Israel’s true Son passes through the water and is tested for forty days.
observation: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand” (3:2).
“I baptize you with water for repentance, but he who is coming after me is mightier than I” (3:11).
“Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness” (3:15).
“This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” (3:17).
“Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil” (4:1).
“It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God” (4:4).
“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men” (4:19).
interpretation:
John’s message is simple: the king is coming, so turn around. The crowds come to be baptized, confessing their sins, but when religious leaders come, John warns them not to rest on being Abraham’s descendants. Fruit, not family, shows repentance.

Then Jesus comes to be baptized, which seems backward. John hesitates, because Jesus has no sins to confess. Jesus says it is fitting “to fulfill all righteousness.” He stands with sinners and takes his place among them, which anticipates the cross. The heavens open, the Spirit descends, and the Father speaks the words that combine Psalm 2 (a royal son) and Isaiah 42 (the servant in whom God delights). Jesus is both the king and the suffering servant.

Immediately the Spirit drives him into the wilderness. Israel failed its testing at hunger, at testing God, and at idolatry. Jesus faces the same three. When he is hungry, he answers with Deuteronomy 8: people live by every word from God’s mouth. When the devil quotes Scripture and tells him to throw himself down, Jesus answers from Deuteronomy 6: do not put the LORD your God to the test. When offered all the kingdoms of the world without a cross, he answers from Deuteronomy 6 again: worship the Lord alone. Every answer is a verse from the book Israel had been given in the wilderness. Jesus succeeds where Israel failed, and he does it by knowing and trusting the word.

Chapter 4 ends with the first disciples leaving their nets and the crowds beginning to gather. The kingdom he announces comes with healing and teaching.
connection: Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1 stand behind the Father’s words at the baptism. Deuteronomy 8:3, 6:16, and 6:13 are the three verses Jesus quotes. Hebrews 4:15 says we have a high priest who in every respect has been tempted as we are, yet without sin. 1 Corinthians 10:1-13 compares Israel’s wilderness failures to our own testing. Ephesians 6:17 calls the word of God the sword of the Spirit.
application:
When you are tempted, answer with a specific verse you know. Choose one this week and memorize it for that purpose.

Notice that Jesus was tempted right after he was told he was God’s beloved Son. Being loved by the Father does not mean being spared trials.

Respond to Jesus’ call to follow. What is one “net” you may need to put down?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for standing with sinners at the Jordan and standing firm in the wilderness.
Ask him to teach you to live by every word from God’s mouth.
Tell him what you are tempted by.
